argument_summary: The most supportable reading of the current record is not that the developer-support migration gap is immaterial, but that certification can proceed only in a caveated form because the release clears aggregate readiness by 2.5 percentage points, had no severity-one launch-rehearsal incidents, and the remaining named-use-case gap is being expressly documented as a limitation with monitoring in the model card and audit packet. That narrows the claim under audit: the basis for certification is aggregate readiness plus explicit disclosure and monitoring, not aggregate readiness alone and not the non-core traffic characterization.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation is costly because it delays the partner launch path even though the release is above aggregate readiness threshold and has no severity-one rehearsal incidents. A narrower disposition avoids unnecessary launch friction while preserving governance discipline: keep the disclosure explicit, preserve monitoring, and avoid reopening the entire certification basis as if general readiness evidence were irrelevant.
claims_about_policy: The policy text does not support treating the non-core or 7% traffic characterization as dispositive because the affected segment is named in a partner launch checklist and legal review remains open. At the same time, the visible audit claim already includes handling the remaining gap through disclosure and monitoring in the model card and audit packet. On this record, the strongest compliant posture is caveated compliance: certification is defendable only if the packet expressly discloses the named-use-case limitation and does not claim the materiality question was resolved by volume or general readiness evidence. Public model-card and AI risk-management guidance support that documentation-and-monitoring posture, though they do not substitute for internal policy predicates.
concessions: Current admissible evidence does not support a clean claim that no material weakness disclosure is required.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one incidents do not by themselves resolve the policy gate for a named launch use case.
There is no approved risk-acceptance record in evidence, and legal review remains open.
The non-core or low-volume characterization is incomplete for materiality under the stated policy.
